measures.title: Net collections
measures.blurb: What actually arrived, against what was billable. This is the number your fee is calculated on.

measures.title: Denial rate
measures.blurb: The share of claims denied, with the reason codes behind them, so you can see the cause and not just the total.

measures.title: Days in AR
measures.blurb: How long money sits before it reaches you, and how much of it has aged past 120 days.
measures.source: Benchmark: the AAFP puts days in AR below 50 at minimum, and 30 to 40 as preferable.

measures.title: First-pass acceptance
measures.blurb: The share of claims accepted on first submission, before anyone has to rework them.

items.q: Do you work inside our existing EHR?
items.a: Yes. We work inside your existing EHR/PM, so there is no software switch and no retraining.
Fourteen days from a signed BAA to steady-state claim submission, in most cases.
No. The engagement is month-to-month, and there are no setup fees.
A percentage of collections, quoted upfront before any work begins.

items.q: Will we lose control of our billing?
items.a: No. We work inside your EHR under accounts you create and can revoke. Every claim, note and payment stays in your system, and the read-only KPI dashboard shows the same numbers we work from. If you leave, there is nothing to hand back.

items.q: What happens to claims already out when we switch?
items.a: They keep moving. We pick up your open AR and the existing work queue on day one, so submissions never stop while onboarding runs.
A BAA is signed before any data moves, and patient records stay in your systems rather than moving into ours.

items.q: Can you take on aged AR cleanup only?
items.a: Yes. Credentialing and AR cleanup can be engaged separately from full billing.
